question: In the sentence, 'The CEO’s behaviour was impeccable', what is the ANTONYM of the word 'impeccable'?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2: Faulty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"impeccable"** refers to something that is flawless, perfect, or free from any fault or error. (निर्दोष, त्रुटिहीन)

 
 
• **Example: **Her performance in the play was impeccable, leaving the audience in awe.
 
 
 
• The word **"faulty"**, which is the antonym of "impeccable," means something that has defects, flaws, or is imperfect. (दोषपूर्ण)
 
 
• **Example: **The faulty wiring in the house caused a short circuit.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'impeccable'** is **'faulty'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2: Faulty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Perfect** (संपूर्ण): Something that is complete, flawless, and without any faults.

 
 
• **Example:** The artist completed the painting with perfect precision.
 
 
 
• **Spotless** (निर्दोष, स्वच्छ): Something that is completely clean or free from any stains, dirt, or flaws.
 
 
• **Example:** Her spotless reputation made her the ideal candidate for the role.
 
 
 
• **Unblemished** (अकलंकित, बेदाग): Something that is free from any kind of marks, flaws, or imperfections.
 
 
• **Example:** The athlete's unblemished record made him a favorite for the award.
